subject: general
question: Which of the following correctly describes the graphical representation of Ohm's law?

options.text: A straight line parallel to x-axis
A straight line through the origin

solution:
The correct answer is __**A straight line through the origin**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ohm's Law** states that the **electric current** flowing through a conductor is **directly proportional** to the **potential difference** (voltage) applied across its ends, provided physical conditions like **temperature** remain constant.
 
• The mathematical formula for this relationship is **V = IR**, where **V** represents the **Voltage**, **I** represents the **Current**, and **R** is the **Resistance** of the conductor.
 
• When plotting a graph with **Voltage (V)** on the y-axis and **Current (I)** on the x-axis, the relationship takes the form of a linear equation **y = mx**, where **m** (the slope) corresponds to the **Resistance (R)**.
 
• Because the current is exactly zero when there is no potential difference, the graphical representation is a **straight line** that must pass through the **origin (0,0)**. ***Hence, option 4 is correct.***
 
• A **hyperbolic curve** would represent an inverse relationship, and a **parallel line** would suggest that one variable is constant regardless of the other, neither of which describes **Ohmic behavior**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Ohmic Conductors:**
 
 
• These are materials that strictly obey **Ohm's Law**. Examples include most metals like **Copper**, **Silver**, and **Aluminum**.
 
• For these materials, the **Resistance** remains constant regardless of the applied voltage or current flow, as long as the **temperature** is stable.
 
 
 
• **Non-Ohmic Conductors:**
 
 
• These materials do not show a linear relationship between **V and I**. Their V-I graph is usually a **curve** rather than a straight line.
 
• Common examples include **semiconductors**, **diodes**, **transistors**, and **electrolyte solutions**.
 
• In these cases, the **Resistance** changes as the current or voltage changes.
 
 
 
• **Significance of the Slope:**
 
 
• In a **V-I graph**, the **slope** (V/I) gives the **Resistance** of the component.
 
• In an **I-V graph**, the **slope** (I/V) gives the **Conductance**, which is the reciprocal of resistance.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Units of Measurement:** The SI unit of **Potential Difference** is the **Volt (V)**, **Current** is measured in **Amperes (A)**, and **Resistance** is measured in **Ohms (Ω)**.
 
• **Historical Context:** The law was named after the German physicist **George Simon Ohm**, who published his findings in his **1827** treatise.
 
• **Factors Affecting Resistance:** Resistance depends on the **nature of the material**, the **length** of the conductor (directly proportional), and the **area of cross-section** (inversely proportional).
 
• **Limitations:** Ohm's law is not a universal law of nature; it is an empirical description of the behavior of certain materials. It fails at very **high frequencies** or when the material undergoes **thermal changes** due to excessive current.
